newsitem.title: USA: Families to sue in Millon Ecuador disaster.
newsitem.headline: Families to sue in Millon Ecuador disaster.

text.p: Attorneys in Miami will soon file lawsuits over the tragic crash of a Millon Air cargo aircraft that last week slammed into a crowded neighborhood in Manta, Ecuador, killing 25 people, an attorney said Tuesday.
"We are representing five families so far," said Miami attorney Aaron Podhurst, "We plan to file a suit relatively soon." Repeated calls to Millon were not returned.
On Oct. 22, a 29 year-old Millon Boeing Co 707 crashed into a residential neighborhood, killing 25, injuring at least 60 and destroying homes and other buildings.
The three crew members were also killed.
The Federal Aviation Administration asked Millon to suspend operations Thursday night and it voluntarily grounded its aircraft. The FAA had not yet taken formal action against Millon.
Podhurst said it was likely that Millon would be named in the suit, but added, "We are just in the preliminary stages of our investigation and cannot say for certain."
"These are some really terrible cases. Some of these people are badly burned," said Podhurst.
Podhurst said he had not yet decided whether the suit would be filed in Florida state or federal court.
Privately-held Millon is an all-cargo carrier based in Miami and flies only to Latin America.
Last year one of the carrier's aircraft slid off a runway in Guatemala City, killing six people on the ground.
